The Savoy Male and Female College

Chapter III therefore describes the early years of Savoy College, 1876-1880, setting forth its aims and objectives from the point of view of those immediately connected with it.

Chapter IV, the main chapter from the chronological viewpoint, traces the expansion of the College in its administration, curriculum, equipment, and enrollment—from its incorporation in 1880 to its close in 1890. Numerous original documents are recorded through photostats and transcript in the interest of completeness and authenticity.

Chapter V, of interest sociologically, undertakes to picture the student life of the College—not uncritically, not abstractly, but rather as the campus activities of the period have been brought to life for the author first hand through the memories of those who participated in and observed them themselves. The present generation will doubtless find the campus life not so different from that of today. Some things in the mores now, however, were strictly taboo by the older forms of fifty years ago. These things, brought back in reminiscent stories, were then in a transitory state and there is found in the narrative illustration of the clearly marked evidence of "compensation" or "substitution."

Chapter VI is a chapter of biography. It presents comments on the trustees and faculty members of The Savoy Male and Female College. A biographical-pictorial Souvenir of Texas in 1889 reveal a constant recurrence of stories of the return and the social foundation upon which this institution was built, a brief sketch of its origin, the list of known trustees and faculty members of the College. Other books have served as comparative data only.
